metadata.title: Identifying Conditional Causal Effects in MPDAGs

extraction_notes.note: The MPDAGs of all examples and the dependency map of Appendix F are TikZ figures (the map is omitted in this source); examples refer to graphs not present as text.

Proof-sketch environments carry rigor semi_formal per the proof-sketch rule although rigor is otherwise not set on proofs. PP5 is the only proof given for Theorem 6 (it combines appendix lemmas), so its proves edge is not alternative.
Numbered equation (2) is Perkovic's (2020) unconditional identification formula stated in full; retyped from equation to theorem with origin external.
Lemmas attributed with 'cf.' to prior work but re-proved here; marked external (attributed result), their proofs paper.
Inline 'We show that ...' openers at the start of labelled proof parts were treated as the label's own goal: the label step is the parent and no separate claim parent was created.
Examples 13-14 contain complete non-identifiability arguments (SEM constructions and expectation computations); kept as examples illustrating Theorem 7 rather than split into claim plus proof.
Within-proof step-to-step dependency edges (edge pass 4) were not added for this long appendix; proofs' dependencies on lemmas are recorded at the proof level and by \ref edges into steps.
Notation conventions (capital letters for nodes, bold for node sets) and the prose description of CIDM in Section 5.1 (which narrates the pseudocode) are not separate nodes.

nodes.name: Graph
nodes.statement: A \textit{graph} $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ consists of a set of nodes $\mb{V}$ and a set of edges $\mb{E}$.

nodes.name: Directed graph
nodes.statement: A \emph{directed graph} contains only directed edges ($\to$).

nodes.name: Partially directed graph
nodes.statement: A \emph{partially directed} graph may contain undirected edges ($-$) and directed edges ($\to$).

nodes.name: Induced subgraph
nodes.statement: An \textit{induced subgraph} $\g_{\mb{V'}} =(\mb{V'}, \mb{E'})$ of $\g$ consists of $\mb{V'} \subseteq \mb{V}$ and $\mb{E'} \subseteq \mb{E}$ where $\mb{E'}$ are all edges in $\mb{E}$ between nodes in $\mb{V'}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{G}_{V'}$: the subgraph on node subset $V'$ with all edges of $\mathcal{G}$ among $V'$.

nodes.name: Edge into / out of a node
nodes.statement: In a partially directed graph, an edge is \textit{into} (\textit{out of}) a node $X$ if the edge is directed and has an arrowhead (tail) at $X$.

nodes.name: Path
nodes.statement: For disjoint node sets $\mb{X}$ and $\mb{Y}$, a \textit{path} from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ is a sequence of distinct nodes $\langle X, \dots,Y \rangle$ from some $X \in \mb{X}$ to some $Y \in \mb{Y}$ for which every pair of successive nodes is adjacent.
differentia: every pair of successive nodes is adjacent

nodes.name: Undirected path
nodes.statement: An \textit{undirected path} is a path containing only undirected edges ($-$).

nodes.name: Directed path
nodes.statement: A \textit{directed path} from $X$ to $Y$ is a path of the form $X \to \dots\to Y$.

nodes.name: Directed cycle
nodes.statement: A directed path from $X$ to $Y$ and the edge $Y\to X$ form a \textit{directed cycle}.

nodes.name: Proper path
nodes.statement: A path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ is \textit{proper} (w.r.t. $\mb{X}$) if only its first node is in $\mb{X}$.
differentia: only its first node is in $\mb{X}$

nodes.name: Possibly directed path
nodes.statement: In a graph $\g$, the  path $p := \langle V_0, \dots, V_k \rangle$, $k \geq 1$, is \textit{possibly directed} if no edge $V_i \gets V_j, 0 \le i < j \le k$, is in $\g$ (\citealp{perkovic2017interpreting}).
differentia: no edge $V_i \gets V_j, 0 \le i < j \le k$, is in $\g$
nodes.statement_short: A path is possibly directed if no edge on it points backward between any two of its nodes.

nodes.name: Subsequence of a path
nodes.statement: A \textit{subsequence} of a path $p$ in a graph $\g$ is a path obtained by deleting a set of non-endpoint nodes from $p$ without changing the order of the remaining nodes.

nodes.name: Subpath
nodes.statement: For a path $p = \langle X_1, \dots, X_m \rangle$, the \textit{subpath} from $X_i$ to $X_k$, for $1 \le i < k \le m$, is the path $p(X_i,X_k) = \langle X_i,X_{i+1}, \dots, X_{k}\rangle$.

nodes.name: Reversed path notation
nodes.statement: We use the notation $(-p)(X_k,X_i)$ to denote the path $\langle X_{k}, X_{k-1}, \dots, X_i \rangle$.

nodes.name: Unshielded triple
nodes.statement: The subpath $\langle X_{j-1}, X_j, X_{j+1} \rangle$, for $1<j<k$, is an \emph{unshielded triple} if $X_{j-1}$ and $X_{j+1}$ are not adjacent in $\g$.

nodes.name: Unshielded path
nodes.statement: A path is \textit{unshielded} if all successive triples on the path are unshielded.

nodes.name: Endpoints of a path
nodes.statement: The \textit{endpoints} of a path $p = \langle X_1, \dots, X_k \rangle$ in a graph $\g$ are the nodes $X_1$ and $X_k$.

nodes.name: Collider
nodes.statement: The node $X_i$, $1 < i < k$, is a \textit{collider} on $p$ if $p$ contains $X_{i-1} \to X_i \gets X_{i+1}$.

nodes.name: Definite non-collider
nodes.statement: The node $X_i$ is a \textit{definite non-collider} on $p$ if $p$ contains $X_{i-1} \gets X_i$ or $X_i \to X_{i+1}$, or if $\langle X_{i-1}, X_i, X_{i+1} \rangle$ is undirected and unshielded.

nodes.name: Node of definite status
nodes.statement: A node is of \textit{definite status} on $p$ if it is an endpoint, collider, or definite non-collider on $p$.

nodes.name: Definite status path
nodes.statement: The path $p$ is of definite status if every node on $p$ is of definite status.

nodes.name: Parent
nodes.statement: If a graph $\g$ contains the edge $X \to Y$, then $X$ is a \textit{parent} of $Y$ in $\g$.

nodes.name: Possible parent
nodes.statement: If $\g$ contains $X - Y$ or $X \to Y$, then $X$ is a \textit{possible parent} of $Y$ in $\g$.

nodes.name: Ancestor and descendant
nodes.statement: If $\g$ contains a directed path from $X$ to $Y$, then $X$ is an \textit{ancestor} of $Y$ and $Y$ is a \textit{descendant} of $X$ in $\g$.

nodes.name: Possible ancestor and possible descendant
nodes.statement: If $\g$ contains a possibly directed path from $X$ to $Y$, then $X$ is a \textit{possible ancestor} of $Y$ and $Y$ is a \textit{possible descendant} of $X$ in $\g$.

nodes.name: Reflexivity convention for ancestral relations
nodes.statement: We use the convention that every node is an ancestor, descendant, possible ancestor, and possible descendant of itself.

nodes.name: Pa, An, De, PossPa, PossAn, PossDe notation
nodes.statement: The sets of parents, ancestors, and descendants and the sets of possible parents, ancestors, and descendants of $X$ in $\g$ are denoted by $\mathrm{Pa}(X,\g)$, $\mathrm{An}(X,\g)$, $\mathrm{De}(X,\g)$, $\mathrm{PossPa}(X,\g)$, $\mathrm{PossAn}(X,\g)$, and $\mathrm{PossDe}(X,\g)$, respectively.

nodes.name: Ancestral sets of node sets
nodes.statement: For a set of nodes $\mb{X}$, we let $\mathrm{An}(\mb{X},\g) = \cup_{X \in \mb{X}} \mathrm{An}(X,\g)$, with analogous definitions for $\mathrm{De}(\mb{X},\g)$, $\mathrm{PossAn}(\mb{X},\g)$, and $\mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X},\g)$.

nodes.name: Parents of a node set
nodes.statement: Unconventionally, we define $\mathrm{Pa}(\mb{X},\g) =(\cup_{X \in \mb{X}} \mathrm{Pa}(X,\g)) \setminus \mb{X}$.
nodes.statement_short: Parents of a set exclude the set itself: Pa(X) is the union of members' parents minus X.

nodes.name: Directed acyclic graph (DAG)
nodes.statement: A directed graph without directed cycles is a \textit{directed acyclic graph (DAG)}.

nodes.name: Partially directed acyclic graph (PDAG)
nodes.statement: A partially directed graph without directed cycles is a \textit{partially directed acyclic graph (PDAG)}.

nodes.name: Completed PDAG (CPDAG)
nodes.statement: All DAGs over a node set $\mb{V}$ with the same adjacencies and unshielded colliders can be uniquely \textit{represented by} a \textit{completed PDAG} (CPDAG).

nodes.name: Maximally oriented PDAG (MPDAG)
nodes.statement: A \textit{maximally oriented PDAG} (MPDAG) is formed by taking a CPDAG, adding background knowledge (by directing undirected edges), and completing \cite{meek1995causal}'s orientation rules.
nodes.statement_short: An MPDAG is a CPDAG with background-knowledge orientations added and closed under Meek's rules.

nodes.name: DAG represented by an MPDAG; the class [G]
nodes.statement: We say a DAG is \textit{represented by} an MPDAG $\g$ if it has the same nodes, adjacencies, and directed edges as $\g$ and if it has no additional unshielded colliders from those in $\g$.
nodes.statement_short: A DAG is represented by an MPDAG if it shares its nodes, adjacencies and directed edges and adds no unshielded colliders.

nodes.name: Restricted equivalence class [G]
nodes.statement: The set of such DAGs---denoted by $[\g]$---forms a restriction of the Markov equivalence class so that all DAGs in $[\g]$ have same set of d-separations.

nodes.name: Undirected MPDAG edges admit both orientations
nodes.statement: Note that if $\g$ has the edge $A - B$, then $[\g]$ contains at least one DAG with $A \to B$ and one DAG with $A \gets B$ \citep{meek1995causal}.
assumptions: $\g$ has the edge $A - B$
conclusions: $[\g]$ contains at least one DAG with $A \to B$ and one DAG with $A \gets B$

nodes.name: All DAGs and CPDAGs are MPDAGs
nodes.statement: Further, note that all DAGs and CPDAGs are MPDAGs.
conclusions: all DAGs and CPDAGs are MPDAGs

nodes.name: Markov compatible density (DAG)
nodes.statement: An \textit{observational density} $f(\mb{v})$ is \textit{Markov compatible} with a DAG $\g[D] = (\mb{V},\mb{E})$ if $f(\mb{v})= \prod_{V_i \in \mb{V}}f(v_i|\mathrm{pa}(v_i,\g[D]))$.

nodes.name: Markov compatibility is preserved under Markov equivalence
nodes.statement: If $f(\mb{v})$ is Markov compatible with a DAG $\g[D]$, then it is Markov compatible with every DAG that is Markov equivalent to $\g[D]$ \citep{pearl2009causality}.
assumptions: $f(\mb{v})$ is Markov compatible with a DAG $\g[D]$
conclusions: it is Markov compatible with every DAG that is Markov equivalent to $\g[D]$

nodes.name: Markov compatible density (MPDAG)
nodes.statement: Hence, we say that a density is \textit{Markov compatible} with an MPDAG $\g$ if it is Markov compatible with a DAG represented by $\g$.

nodes.name: Positivity
nodes.statement: Throughout, we assume positivity. That is, we only consider densities that satisfy $f(\mb{v})>0$ for all valid values of $\mb{V}$ \citep{kivva2023identifiability}.

nodes.name: d-connecting (open) path
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{X}$, $\mb{Y}$, and $\mb{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a graph $\g$. A definite status path \textit{p} from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ is \textit{d-connecting} (or \textit{open}) given $\mb{Z}$ if every definite non-collider on $p$ is not in $\mb{Z}$ and every collider on $p$ has a descendant in $\mb{Z}$.
differentia: every definite non-collider on $p$ is not in $\mb{Z}$
every collider on $p$ has a descendant in $\mb{Z}$

nodes.name: Blocked path
nodes.statement: Otherwise, $p$ is \textit{blocked} given $\mb{Z}$.

nodes.name: d-separation
nodes.statement: If all definite status paths between $\mb{X}$ and $\mb{Y}$ in $\g$ are blocked given $\mb{Z}$, then $\mb{X}$ is \textit{d-separated} from $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ in $\g$ and we write $(\mb{X} \perp_{d} \mb{Y} | \mb{Z})_{\g}$.

nodes.name: Global Markov property of d-separation
nodes.statement: This d-separation implies that $\mb{X}$ and $\mb{Y}$ are conditionally independent given $\mb{Z}$ in any \textit{observational density} that is Markov compatible with $\g$ \citep{lauritzen1990independence, henckel2022graphical}.
nodes.origin_citation: Lauritzen et al. 1990; Henckel et al. 2022
conclusions: $\mb{X}$ and $\mb{Y}$ are conditionally independent given $\mb{Z}$ in any \textit{observational density} that is Markov compatible with $\g$

nodes.name: Causal MPDAG
nodes.statement: An MPDAG $\g$ is a \textit{causal MPDAG} if every edge $V_i \to V_j$ in $\g$ represents a direct causal effect of $V_i$ on $V_j$ and if every edge $V_i - V_j$ represents a direct causal effect of unknown direction (either $V_i$ causes $V_j$ or $V_j$ causes $V_i$).

nodes.name: Causal, possibly causal and non-causal paths
nodes.statement: In a causal MPDAG, any directed path is \textit{causal}, any possibly directed path is \textit{possibly causal}, and any other path is \textit{non-causal}.

nodes.name: Total causal ordering
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{X} = \{X_1, \dots, X_k\}$, $k \ge 1$, be a node set in a causal DAG $\g[D]$. We say that $X_1 < \dots < X_k$ is a \textit{total causal ordering} of $\mb{X}$ consistent with $\g[D]$ if for every $X_i, X_j \in \mb{X}$ such that $X_i < X_j$ and such that $X_i$ and $X_j$ are adjacent in $\g[D]$, then $\g[D]$ contains $X_i \to X_j$.

nodes.name: Partial causal ordering
nodes.statement: Now let $\mb{X}$ be a node set in a causal MPDAG $\g$. Since $\g$ may contain undirected edges, there is generally no total causal ordering of $\mb{X}$ consistent with $\g$. Instead, we define a \textit{partial causal ordering} of $\mb{X}$ consistent with $\g$ to be an ordering of pairwise disjoint node sets $\mb{A_1}, \dots, \mb{A_k}$, $k \ge 1$, $\cup_{i=1}^k \mb{A_i} = \mb{X}$, that satisfies the following: for every $i,j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ such that $\mb{A_i} < \mb{A_j}$ and there is an edge between $A_i \in \mb{A_i}$ and $A_j \in \mb{A_j}$ in $\g$, then $\g$ contains $A_i \to A_j$.
nodes.genus: ordering of pairwise disjoint node sets
nodes.statement_short: An ordering A_1<...<A_k of disjoint node sets covering X such that every edge between earlier and later sets points forward.

nodes.name: Observational density f(v)
nodes.statement: Let $f(\mb{v})$ be an observational density over a set of variables $\mb{V}$.

nodes.name: do-intervention notation
nodes.statement: The notation $do(\mb{X} = \mb{x})$, or $do(\mb{x})$ for short, represents an outside intervention that sets $\mb{X} \subseteq \mb{V}$ to fixed values $\mb{x}$.

nodes.name: Interventional density
nodes.statement: An \textit{interventional density} $f(\mb{v}|do(\mb{x}))$ is a density resulting from such an intervention.

nodes.name: Set of all interventional densities F*
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{F^*}$ denote the set of all interventional densities $f(\mb{v}|do(\mb{x}))$ such that $\mb{X} \subseteq \mb{V}$ (including $\mb{X} = \emptyset$).

nodes.name: Causal Bayesian network compatible with F* (truncated factorization)
nodes.statement_short: A causal DAG is compatible with F* iff every interventional density factorizes by the truncated factorization over non-intervened nodes.

nodes.name: Truncated factorization
nodes.statement: f(\mb{v} | do(\mb{x})) = \prod_{V_i \in \mb{V} \setminus \mb{X}} f(v_i|\mathrm{pa}(v_i,\g[D])) \mathbbm{1}(\mb{X} = \mb{x})
nodes.label: eq:trunc-fact

nodes.name: Interventional density consistent with a causal DAG
nodes.statement: We say an interventional density is \textit{consistent} with a causal DAG $\g[D]$ if it belongs to a set of interventional densities $\mb{F^*}$ such that $\g[D]$ is compatible with $\mb{F^*}$.

nodes.name: Interventional density consistent with a causal MPDAG
nodes.statement: We say an interventional density is \textit{consistent} with a causal MPDAG $\g$ if it is consistent with each DAG in $[\g]$---were the DAG to be causal.

nodes.name: Identifiability of a conditional causal effect
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{X}$, $\mb{Y}$, and $\mb{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal MPDAG $\g = (\mb{V,E})$, and let $\mb{F^*_i} = \{ f_i(\mb{v}|do(\mb{x'})) : \mb{X'} \subseteq \mb{V} \}$ be a set with which a DAG $\g[D]_i \in [\g]$ is compatible---were $\g[D]_i$ to be causal. Then the conditional causal effect of $\mb{X}$ on $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ is \textit{identifiable} in $\g$ if for any $\mb{F^*_1}, \mb{F^*_2}$ such that $f_1(\mb{v}) = f_2(\mb{v})$, we have $f_1(\mb{y}|do(\mb{x}), \mb{z}) = f_2(\mb{y}|do(\mb{x}), \mb{z})$ \citep{pearl2009causality}.
nodes.statement_short: The effect is identifiable if any two compatible model families with equal observational densities give the same conditional interventional density.

nodes.name: PCO Algorithm output (ordered bucket decomposition)
nodes.statement: The PCO Algorithm inputs a set of nodes from an MPDAG and outputs an ordered partition of that node set, which we call an \textit{ordered bucket decomposition}. That is, if $\mb{D}$ is a node set in an MPDAG $\g$, then $\text{PCO}(\mb{D},\g) = (\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k})$, $k \ge 1$, where $\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k}$ are pairwise disjoint subsets of $\g[D]$ that follow a \textit{partial causal ordering} consistent with $\g$ (see Section \ref{sec:prelims}).
nodes.statement_short: PCO(D,G) returns an ordered partition (B_1,...,B_k) of D following a partial causal ordering consistent with G.

nodes.name: Bucket
nodes.genus: intersection of $\mb{D}$ with a maximal undirected connected set in $\g$
nodes.statement_short: A bucket in D is the intersection of D with a maximal undirected connected component of the MPDAG.
nodes.label: def:bucket

nodes.name: Ordered Bucket Decomposition
nodes.statement_short: A tuple of buckets partitioning D, ordered so that every edge between different buckets points from earlier to later.
nodes.label: def:obd

nodes.name: Conditional Identification Formula
assumptions: $\mb{X}$, $\mb{Y}$, and $\mb{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal MPDAG $\g =(\mb{V,E})$
$\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X},\g) = \emptyset$
there is no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ in $\g$ that starts with an undirected edge
nodes.statement_short: If Z is not a possible descendant of X and no proper possibly causal X-to-Y path starts undirected, f(y|do(x),z) is an integral of bucket-wise conditionals from the PCO decomposition.
nodes.label: thm:id-formula

nodes.name: Conditional identification formula
nodes.statement: f(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}),\mb{z}) = \int \prod_{i\in \mb{I_E}} f(\mb{b_i} \,|\, \mathrm{pa}(\mb{b_i},\g)) \prod_{i \in \mb{I_N}} f(\mb{b_i} \,|\, \mb{b_i^N}, \mb{z}) \ \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mb{b},
nodes.label: eq:id-formula

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (Conditional Identification Formula)
nodes.statement_short: Law of total probability and chain rule over the buckets, then Lemma 38 replaces each bucket factor.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Lemma 38
nodes.statement_short: Apply Pearl's do-calculus Rules 1-3 in an arbitrary DAG of [G]; the needed d-separations hold since no possibly causal path leaves B_i towards earlier variables.

nodes.name: Bucket-wise factor identity (Lemma 38 claim)

nodes.name: Unconditional formula as special case (Z empty)
nodes.statement: To compare Equations \eqref{eq:id-formula} and \eqref{eq:id-formula-unconditional}, we note that Theorem \ref{thm:id-formula} holds for any conditioning set $\mb{Z}$, including when $\mb{Z} = \emptyset$. In this case, ${\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{B_i}, \g) = \emptyset}$ for all $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, and thus, Equation \eqref{eq:id-formula} reduces to the exact form of the unconditional identification formula shown in Equation \eqref{eq:id-formula-unconditional}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement:
Let $\g[D]$ be an arbitrary DAG in $[\g]$. The result holds by Rule 3 of the do calculus (Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc}, App. \ref{app:existing}) if we show $(\mb{Y} \perp_{d} \mb{X} \,|\, \mb{Z})_{\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{W}}}}$ for $\mb{W} := \mb{X} \setminus \mathrm{An}(\mb{Z}, \g[D])$. Note that $\mathrm{De}(\mb{X}, \g[D]) \subseteq \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g)$ (Lemma \ref{lem:pc-imply2}, App. \ref{app:mpdags}) so that $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g) = \emptyset$ implies $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{De}(\mb{X}, \g[D]) = \emptyset$. Thus, $\mb{W} = \mb{X}$ and we must show $(\mb{Y} \perp_{d} \mb{X} \,|\, \mb{Z})_{\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}}$.

    Let $p$ be an arbitrary path in $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ from $X \in \mb{X}$ to $Y \in \mb{Y}$. By definition of $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$, $p$ begins $X \to$. But $p$ cannot be causal, since this would imply $Y \in \mathrm{De}(\mb{X}, \g[D]) \subseteq \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g)$, which is a contradiction. Thus, $p$ must have a collider. Form a set $\mb{S}$ with the collider on $p$ that is closest to $X$ on $p$ and all of its descendants in $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$. Since $\mb{S} \subseteq \mathrm{De}(X, \g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}) \subseteq \mathrm{De}(\mb{X}, \g[D]) \subseteq \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g)$ and since $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g) = \emptyset$, then $p$ must be d-separated given $\mb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Rule 3 in an arbitrary DAG; any path from X to Y in the mutilated DAG has a collider whose descendants avoid Z.

nodes.name: Conditional Adjustment
nodes.statement:
Let $\g$ be the causal MPDAG in Figure \ref{fig:ex1}\subref{fig:ex-id-cas}, and let $\mb{X} = \{X\}$, $\mb{Y}=\{Y\}$, and $\mb{Z}=\{V_1\}$. To use Theorem \ref{thm:id-formula}, we confirm $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g) = \emptyset$ and no possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ starts undirected. Then we find $\mb{B_1}=\{V_2\}$ (where $1 \in \mb{I_N}$), $\mb{B_2}=\{Y\}$ (where $2 \in \mb{I_E}$), and $\mb{B}= \{V_2\}$. Thus for $f$ consistent with $\g$,
    \vskip -.6cm
    \begin{align*}
        f(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}),\mb{z})
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f\big(\mb{b_2} \,|\, \mathrm{pa}(\mb{b_2},\g)\big)\, f(\mb{b_1} \,|\, \mb{b_1^N},\mb{z}) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mb{b} \\
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f(y \,|\, x, v_1, v_2) \,f(v_2 \,|\, v_1) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} v_2.
    \end{align*}
    Compare this to Example 2 of \cite{laplante2024conditional}, where the authors find the identical form of $f(\mb{y}|do(\mb{x}),\mb{z})$ by showing that $\mb{S} := \{V_2\}$ is a conditional adjustment set.
nodes.label: ex:id-cas

nodes.name: No Conditional Adjustment
nodes.statement:
Let $\g$ be the causal DAG (and therefore, MPDAG) in Figure \ref{fig:ex1}\subref{fig:ex-id-nocas}, and let $\mb{X} = \{X_1, X_2\}$, $\mb{Y}=\{Y\}$, and $\mb{Z}=\{V_2\}$. To use Theorem \ref{thm:id-formula}, we confirm $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g) = \emptyset$ and no possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ starts undirected. Then we find $\mb{B_1}=\{V_1\}$, $\mb{B_2}=\{Y\}$ (where $1,2 \in \mb{I_E}$), and $\mb{B}= \{V_1\}$. Thus for $f$ consistent with $\g$,
    \vskip -.6cm
    \begin{align}
        f(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}),\mb{z})
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f\big(\mb{b_1} \,|\, \mathrm{pa}(\mb{b_1},\g)\big) \,f\big(\mb{b_2} \,|\, \mathrm{pa}(\mb{b_2},\g)\big) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mb{b} \nonumber\\
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f(v_1 \,|\, x_1) \,f(y \,|\, x_2, v_1, v_2) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} v_1. \nonumber
    \end{align}
    Note that \cite{laplante2024conditional} show there is no conditional adjustment set in this case (see their Figure 4).
nodes.label: ex:id-nocas

nodes.name: Identifiability Condition, Restricted Z
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{X}$, $\mb{Y}$, and $\mb{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal MPDAG $\g$ such that $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X},\g) = \emptyset$. Then the conditional causal effect of $\mb{X}$ on $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ is identifiable in $\g$ if and only if there is no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ in $\g$ that starts with an undirected edge.

$\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X},\g) = \emptyset$
conclusions: the conditional causal effect of $\mb{X}$ on $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ is identifiable in $\g$ if and only if there is no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ in $\g$ that starts with an undirected edge
equivalent_conditions: the conditional causal effect of $\mb{X}$ on $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ is identifiable in $\g$
there is no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ in $\g$ that starts with an undirected edge

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Proposition 5
nodes.statement: The proof of Proposition \ref{prop:id-condition} can be found in Appendix \ref{app:id-condition}, but we provide an outline here for intuition. Note that $\Leftarrow$ follows from Theorem \ref{thm:id-formula}. We show $\Rightarrow$ through its contraposition. Thus, suppose there is a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ in $\g$ that starts undirected. We show in a separate result (Lemma \ref{lem:twopaths-corrollary}, App. \ref{app:id-condition}) that this path implies there are DAGs $\g[D]^1,\g[D]^2 \in [\g]$ with corresponding paths $X \to \dots \to Y$ and $X \gets V_1 \to \dots \to Y$. To show the conditional effect is not identifiable, we find $\{ f_1(\mb{v}|do(\mb{x'})) : \mb{X'} \subseteq \mb{V} \}$ and $\{ f_2(\mb{v}|do(\mb{x'})) : \mb{X'} \subseteq \mb{V} \}$ that are compatible with $\g[D]^1$ and $\g[D]^2$, where $f_1(\mb{v})=f_2(\mb{v})$ but $f_1(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{z}) \neq f_2(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{z})$. We construct these sets using structural equation models (SEMs) based on DAGs with the same nodes as $\g[D]^i$ but with only the edges from the path of interest. To complete the proof, we show $E_1[Y | do(\mb{X}=\mb{1}), \mb{Z}] \neq E_2[Y | do(\mb{X}=\mb{1}), \mb{Z}]$ using the relevant DAGs, the do calculus (Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc}, App. \ref{app:existing}), and Wright's Rule (Lemma \ref{lem:wright}).
nodes.statement_short: Sufficiency from Theorem 3; necessity by contraposition, building two linear Gaussian SEMs on DAGs of [G] with equal observational but different conditional interventional densities.

nodes.name: Mutilated DAG (edges into X removed)
nodes.statement: For example, $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ denotes the graph obtained by taking $\g[D]$ and removing all edges into $\mb{X}$.

nodes.name: Mutilated MPDAG (edges into X removed)
nodes.statement: For example, we use $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ to denote the graph obtained by taking $\g$ and removing all edges into $\mb{X}$.

nodes.name: Mutilated MPDAGs differ from Pearl's mutilated DAGs
nodes.statement: But this process differs from Pearl's in several ways. First, removing edges from $\g$ into $\mb{X}$ does not have the same intuitive relationship with the intervention $do(\mb{x})$, since $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ may still contain edges adjacent to $\mb{X}$ that are undirected. In the true causal DAG, the corresponding edges may be directed into $\mb{X}$ and thus, represent a causal effect on $\mb{X}$. Second, these mutilated graphs may no longer be MPDAGs. For example, consider an MPDAG $\g$ that contains the paths $V_1 \to V_2 - X$ and $V_1 \to X$. The graph $\g_{\overline{X}}$ only contains the path $V_1 \to V_2 - X$, and thus, is not closed under \citeauthor{meek1995causal}'s (\citeyear{meek1995causal}) orientation rules.
nodes.statement_short: Removing edges into X from an MPDAG leaves undirected edges at X and may yield a graph that is not an MPDAG.

nodes.statement_short: Pearl's three do-calculus rules hold for densities consistent with a causal MPDAG, with d-separations read in mutilated MPDAGs.
nodes.label: thm:do-calc-mpdag

nodes.name: Rule 1 for MPDAGs (insertion/deletion of observations)
nodes.statement: f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{z}, \mb{w}) = f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{w}).
nodes.label: eq:rule1-do-mpdag

nodes.name: Rule 2 for MPDAGs (action/observation exchange)
nodes.statement: f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{z}), \mb{w}, do(\mb{x})) = f(\mb{y} | \mb{z}, \mb{w}, do(\mb{x})).
nodes.label: eq:rule2-do-mpdag

nodes.name: Rule 3 for MPDAGs (insertion/deletion of actions)
nodes.label: eq:rule3-do-mpdag

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 6 (Do Calculus for MPDAGs)
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc-mpdag} follows from the do calculus of \cite{pearl2009causality} as well as Lemmas \ref{lem:zhang-modify-1b}, \ref{lem:zhang-modify-2b}, and \ref{lem:zhang-modify-3c}. These lemmas and their proofs can be found in Appendix \ref{app:do}, but we provide an overview here for intuition. Consider Rule 1 as an example. The result follows directly from Lemma \ref{lem:zhang-modify-1b}, which claims that if the given d-separation---$\mb{Y} \perp_{d} \mb{Z} \,|\, \mb{X}, \mb{W}$---holds in the mutilated graph $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$, then the same d-separation will hold in $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ for any DAG $\g[D]$ in the equivalence class $[\g]$. We prove this by contraposition. Thus, we start by assuming there is a DAG $\g[D] \in [\g]$ such that $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ has a path $\overline{p}$ from $\mb{Y}$ to $\mb{Z}$ that is open given $\mb{X} \cup \mb{W}$. By definition, no non-collider on $\overline{p}$ is in $\mb{X} \cup \mb{W}$. We then show that every collider on $\overline{p}$ is in $\mathrm{An}( \mb{X} \cup \mb{W}, \g_{\overline{\mb{X}}} )$. To do this, we draw repeatedly on the relationships between $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$, $\g[D]$, $\g$, and $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$. We prove this implies that the sequence of nodes in $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$ corresponding to $\overline{p}$ forms a path from $\mb{Y}$ to $\mb{Z}$ that is open given $\mb{X} \cup \mb{W}$, which completes the proof. We rely on a similar contraposition for showing that Rules 2 and 3 hold.
nodes.statement_short: Each rule follows from Pearl's do calculus plus a lemma transferring d-separation from the mutilated MPDAG to every mutilated DAG in [G], proved by contraposition.

nodes.name: Do calculus for MPDAGs coincides with Pearl's on DAGs
nodes.statement: Note that since all DAGs are MPDAGs, Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc-mpdag} holds when a full DAG is known. We want to highlight that our do calculus and \citeauthor{pearl2009causality}'s are identical in this case.
assumptions: a full DAG is known
conclusions: our do calculus and \citeauthor{pearl2009causality}'s are identical in this case

nodes.name: Proof that the MPDAG do calculus reduces to Pearl's
nodes.statement: This claim follows without proof after considering a small detail found in Rule 3. Compare the definition of $\mb{Z'(W)}$ from Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc-mpdag} with that of $\mb{Z(W)}$ from Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc}. To show these sets are equivalent when a DAG $\g$ is known, we must show that $\mb{Z} \setminus \mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\mb{V} \setminus \mb{X}}) = \mb{Z} \setminus \mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\overline{\mb{X}}})$. To see this, note that $\mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\mb{V} \setminus \mb{X}}) \subseteq \mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\overline{\mb{X}}})$, where the only variables in $\mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\overline{\mb{X}}})$ not in $\mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\mb{V} \setminus \mb{X}})$ are in $\mb{X}$. But $\mb{Z}$ and $\mb{X}$ are disjoint. Therefore, removing $\mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\mb{V} \setminus \mb{X}})$ from $\mb{Z}$ is equivalent to removing $\mathrm{An}(\mb{W}, \g_{\overline{\mb{X}}})$ from $\mb{Z}$, and the claim holds.
nodes.statement_short: Show Z'(W) equals Pearl's Z(W) for a DAG: the two ancestor sets differ only by nodes in X, which is disjoint from Z.

nodes.name: Multiple Routes
nodes.statement:
Reconsider Example \ref{ex:id-cas}, where we found the form of a conditional effect using our identification formula. We could instead use Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc-mpdag}:
    \begin{align*}
        f(\mb{y}|do(\mb{x}),\mb{z})
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f(y, v_2|do(x), v_1) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} v_2 \\
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f(y|do(x), v_1, v_2) \,f(v_2|do(x), v_1) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} v_2 \\
            &=\scaleobj{.6}{\int} \,f(y|x, v_1, v_2) \,f(v_2|v_1) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} v_2,
    \end{align*}
    The first two equalities hold by the law of total probability and the chain rule, respectively. The third holds by Rules 2 and 3, since $Y \perp_{d} X \,|\, V_1,V_2$ in $\g_{\underline{\mb{X}}}$ and $V_2 \perp_{d} X \,|\, V_1$ in $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$. This example provides a case where all three methods---conditional adjustment, the identification formula, and the do calculus for MPDAGs---find the same form for the conditional effect.
nodes.label: ex:do-multi

nodes.name: Not Identifiable
nodes.statement: Let $\g$ be the causal MPDAG in Figure \ref{fig:ex-alg}\subref{fig:ex-alg-c}, and let $\mb{X} = \{X\}$, $\mb{Y} = \{Y\}$, and $\mb{Z} = \{Z\}$. To use Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm}, we first consider the \emph{\texttt{while}} loop of lines \ref{alg:cidm-a}-\ref{alg:cidm-b}. Note that there is a possibly causal path from $X \in \mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y} \cup \mb{Z}$ that starts undirected, but $\mb{Y} \not\perp_{d} X \,|\, \mb{Z}$ in $\g_{\underline{X}}$. Thus, the algorithm returns a \emph{\texttt{FAIL}}. In Section \ref{sec:alg-condition}, we show this effect is not identifiable in $\g$ (see Example \ref{ex:alg-condition1}).
nodes.label: ex:alg-fail1

nodes.name: Reduces to Identification Formula
nodes.statement: Reconsider Example \ref{ex:id-cas}, but now use Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm} to identify the causal effect. We skip lines \ref{alg:cidm-a}-\ref{alg:cidm-d}, since the following hold: $\mb{Z} \cap \mathrm{PossDe}(\mb{X}, \g) = \emptyset$, no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ starts undirected, and $\mb{Y} \not\perp_{d} \mb{X} \,|\, \mb{Z}$ in $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$. Thus, the algorithm reduces to lines \ref{alg:cidm-e}-\ref{alg:cidm-i}, and since $\mb{Z^N}=\mb{Z}$, these lines reduce to the same application of our identification formula shown in Example \ref{ex:id-cas}. Note that this logic also applies to Example \ref{ex:id-nocas}.

nodes.name: Reduces to Rule 3
nodes.statement: Reconsider Example \ref{ex:id-rule3}, but now use Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm} to identify the causal effect. We skip lines \ref{alg:cidm-a}-\ref{alg:cidm-b}, since no there is no possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y} \cup \mb{Z}$. From lines \ref{alg:cidm-c}-\ref{alg:cidm-d}, we confirm that $\mb{Y} \perp_{d} \mb{X} \,|\, \mb{Z}$ in $\g_{\overline{\mb{X}}}$. Thus, the algorithm reduces to an application of Rule 3 of our do calculus. In this case, note that this is equivalent to the application of Theorem \ref{thm:id-rule3} shown in Example \ref{ex:id-rule3}.

nodes.name: Reduces to Rule 2
nodes.statement: Reconsider Example \ref{ex:do-rule2}. To use Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm}, we first consider the \emph{\texttt{while}} loop of lines \ref{alg:cidm-a}-\ref{alg:cidm-b}. Since there is a possibly causal path from $X \in \mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y} \cup \mb{Z}$ that starts undirected, we confirm that $\mb{Y} \perp_{d} X \,|\, \mb{Z}$ in $\g_{\underline{X}}$. Thus, we define $\mb{X'} = \emptyset$ and $\mb{Z'} = \{X,Z\}$. Formally, the algorithm must exit the \emph{\texttt{while}} loop and consider lines \ref{alg:cidm-c}-\ref{alg:cidm-d}, but note that it has already found an identifying form (that the additional steps will not change). Thus, the algorithm reduces to the same application of Rule 2 of our do calculus shown in Example \ref{ex:do-rule2}. Additionally note that the same logic applies to Example \ref{ex:do-rule3}.

nodes.name: Soundness of CIDM
nodes.statement: Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm} is sound for identifying conditional causal effects given an MPDAG. That is, any expression the algorithm outputs will be an identifying form of $f(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}), \mb{z})$.
conclusions: Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm} is sound for identifying conditional causal effects given an MPDAG

nodes.name: Proof of soundness of CIDM
nodes.statement: This follows directly from Rules 2-3 of the do calculus for MPDAGs (Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc-mpdag}), the chain rule, our positivity assumption (see Section \ref{sec:prelims}), and our conditional identification formula (Theorem \ref{thm:id-formula}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine Rules 2-3 of the MPDAG do calculus, the chain rule, positivity and the identification formula.

nodes.name: Completeness of Algorithm CIDM
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{X}$, $\mb{Y}$, and $\mb{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal MPDAG $\g$. If there is a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y} \cup \mb{Z}$ in $\g$ that starts with an undirected edge and contains any $X \in \mb{X}$ such that $\mb{Y} \not\perp_{d} X \,|\, \mb{X} \setminus \{X\}, \mb{Z}$ in $\g_{\overline{\mb{X} \setminus \{X\}} \underline{X}}$, then the conditional causal effect of $\mb{X}$ on $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ is not identifiable in $\g$.
assumptions: $\mb{X}$, $\mb{Y}$, and $\mb{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal MPDAG $\g$

there is a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y} \cup \mb{Z}$ in $\g$ that starts with an undirected edge and contains any $X \in \mb{X}$ such that $\mb{Y} \not\perp_{d} X \,|\, \mb{X} \setminus \{X\}, \mb{Z}$ in $\g_{\overline{\mb{X} \setminus \{X\}} \underline{X}}$

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 7
nodes.statement_short: Define the sets S_1, S_2 of d-connecting paths and split on whether S_2 has paths starting directed or undirected; illustrated by two examples.

nodes.name: Sets S_1 and S_2 of d-connecting paths
nodes.label: thm:alg-complete-s2

nodes.name: Path in S_2 that Starts Directed
nodes.statement:
Reconsider Example \ref{ex:alg-fail1}, where we attempted to use Algorithm \ref{alg:cidm} to identify the conditional effect of $\mb{X}$ on $\mb{Y}$ given $\mb{Z}$ but the algorithm output a \texttt{FAIL}. Note that the MPDAG $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ in this example contains the path $X \gets V_1 \to Y$, which belongs to the set $\mb{S_2}$ given in \eqref{thm:alg-complete-s2} and which starts directed.
    
    To show the conditional effect is not identifiable in $\g$, consider the DAGs $\g[D]^1, \g[D]^2 \in [\g]$ shown in Figure \ref{fig:alg-condition1}\subref{fig:alg-condition1-a}-\subref{fig:alg-condition1-b}. It suffices to show that each $\g[D]^i$ is compatible with a family of interventional densities $\mb{F^*_i} = \{ f_i(\mb{v}|do(\mb{x'})) : \mb{X'} \subseteq \mb{V} \}$ such that the following hold.
    \begin{align}
        f_1(\mb{v}) &\,=\, f_2(\mb{v}). \\
        f_1(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}), \mb{z}) & \,\neq\, f_2(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}), \mb{z}). \end{align}

    
    To define such families, consider the DAG $\g[D]^{1'}$ in Figure \ref{fig:alg-condition1}\subref{fig:alg-condition1-c}, and note that $\g[D]^{1'}$ is constructed by removing edges from $\g[D]^1$. Below we build an $\mb{F^*_1}$ such that $\g[D]^{1'}$ is compatible with $\mb{F^*_1}$. It follows that $\g[D]^1$ is compatible with $\mb{F^*_1}$ (see Lemma \ref{lem:markov-sub}, App. \ref{app:id-condition}). Start by considering the following structural equation model (SEM) with independent errors:
    \begin{align}
        V_1       &\gets  \varepsilon_{v_1};                   &\varepsilon_{v_1} &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1); \\
        X   &\gets  \tfrac{1}{2}V_1   +  \varepsilon_x;  &\varepsilon_x &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{3}{4});\nonumber\\
        Z   &\gets  \tfrac{1}{2} V_1 + \tfrac{1}{2} X + \varepsilon_z; &\varepsilon_z &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, \tfrac{1}{4});\nonumber\\
        Y   &\gets  \tfrac{1}{2} V_1 + \varepsilon_y;    &\varepsilon_y &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{3}{4}). \nonumber
    \end{align}
    We build $\mb{F^*_1}$ by letting $f_1(\mb{v})$ be the density of the multivariate normal generated by the SEM in \eqref{ex:alg-condition1-sem1}. For the remaining densities in $\mb{F^*_1}$, we let $f_1(\mb{v} \,|\, do(\mb{x'})) := f_*(\mb{v})$, where $f_*$ is  the density of the multivariate normal generated by taking the SEM in \eqref{ex:alg-condition1-sem1} and replacing $\mb{X'}$ with its interventional value $\mb{x'}$ \citep{pearl2009causality}.


    
    Now consider the DAG $\g[D]^{2'}$ in Figure \ref{fig:alg-condition1}\subref{fig:alg-condition1-d}, and note that $\g[D]^{2'}$ is constructed by removing edges from $\g[D]^2$. Next consider the following SEM with independent errors:
    \begin{align}
        V_1       &\gets  \varepsilon_{v_1};                   &\varepsilon_{v_1} &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1); \\
        X   &\gets  {-\tfrac{1}{7}V_1} + \tfrac{6}{7} Z + \varepsilon_x;  &\varepsilon_x &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{3}{7}); \nonumber\\
        Z   &\gets  \tfrac{3}{4} V_1 + \varepsilon_z;    &\varepsilon_z &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{7}{16}); \nonumber\\
        Y   &\gets  \tfrac{1}{2} V_1 + \varepsilon_y;    &\varepsilon_y &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{3}{4}), \nonumber
    \end{align}
    Just as we built $\mb{F^*_1}$ based on the SEM in \eqref{ex:alg-condition1-sem1}, we build $\mb{F^*_2}$ based on the SEM in \eqref{ex:alg-condition1-sem2}. It follows that $\g[D]^{2'}$---and therefore $\g[D]^2$---is compatible with $\mb{F^*_2}$.


    
    Thus we have two families of interventional densities such that $\g[D]^i$ is compatible with $\mb{F^*_i}$. Further, we can show that $f_1(\mb{v})=f_2(\mb{v})$ so that \eqref{eq:alg-condition1-a} holds. To complete the proof, we show that \eqref{eq:alg-condition1-b} holds. It suffices to show that $E[Y \,|\, do(X=1), Z=0]$ is not the same under $f_1$ and $f_2$. We start by calculating this expectation under $f_2$:    
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}_{f_2}[Y \,|\, do(X=1), Z=0]
            &\,=\, \left. \mathbb{E}_{f_2}[Y \,|\, Z] \,\, \right\rvert_{\, Z=0}\\
            &\,=\, \left. \mathbb{E}_{f_2}[Y] + \frac{\mathrm{Cov}_{f_2}(Y,Z)}{\mathrm{Var}_{f_2}(Z)} \cdot \Big(Z - \mathbb{E}_{f_2}[Z]\Big) \, \right\rvert_{\, Z=0}\\
            &\,=\, \left. \tfrac{3}{8} Z \, \right\rvert_{\, Z=0}\\
            &\,=\, 0.
    \end{align*}
    The first equality follows from \citeauthor{pearl2009causality}'s do calculus (Theorem \ref{thm:do-calc}), since $Y \perp_{d} X \,|\, Z$ in $\g[D]^{2'}_{\overline{X}}$ and since $f_2$ is consistent with $\g[D]^{2'}$. The second equality follows from properties of multivariate normals (see Lemma \ref{lem:mardia}). 
    
    
    To calculate the same expectation under $f_1$, recall that $f_1(\mb{v} \,|\, do(x)) := f_*(\mb{v})$, where $f_*(\mb{v})$ is the multivariate normal density generated by the following SEM with independent errors:
    \begin{align}
        V_1       &\gets  \varepsilon_{v_1};                   &\varepsilon_{v_1} &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1); \\
        X   &\gets  x; \nonumber\\
        Z   &\gets  \tfrac{1}{2} V_1 + \tfrac{1}{2} x + \varepsilon_z; &\varepsilon_z &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, \tfrac{1}{4});\nonumber\\
        Y   &\gets  \tfrac{1}{2} V_1 + \varepsilon_y;    &\varepsilon_y &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{3}{4}), \nonumber
    \end{align}
    It follows that $f_1(y \,|\, do(x),z) := f_*(y \,|\, z)$ is the conditional density of $Y \,|\, Z$ under $f_*(\mb{v})$. Based on this and properties of multivariate normals (see Lemma \ref{lem:mardia}),
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}_{f_1}[Y \,|\, do(X= 1), Z=0]
            &\,=\, \left. \mathbb{E}_{f_*}[Y \,|\, Z] \,\, \right\rvert_{\, x=1, \, Z=0}\\
            &\,=\, \left. \mathbb{E}_{f_*}[Y] + \frac{\mathrm{Cov}_{f_*}(Y,Z)}{\mathrm{Var}_{f_*}(Z)} \cdot \Big(Z - \mathbb{E}_{f_*}[Z]\Big) \, \right\rvert_{\, x=1, \, Z=0}\\
            &\,=\, \left. \tfrac{1}{2} \Big(Z - \frac{1}{2}x \Big) \, \right\rvert_{\, x=1, \, Z=0}\\
            &\,\neq\, 0.
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Two Gaussian SEMs on DAGs of [G] agree observationally but give different E[Y|do(X=1),Z=0], so the effect is not identifiable.
nodes.label: ex:alg-condition1

nodes.name: Path in S_2 that Starts Undirected
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian SEMs on the two orientations of X - V_1 give different E[Y|do(X=1),Z=0], showing non-identifiability.
nodes.label: ex:alg-condition2

nodes.name: Conditional Identification for MPDAGs + Enumeration (CIDME)
input: Disjoint node sets $\mb{X}, \mb{Y}, \mb{Z} \subseteq \mb{V}$ and causal MPDAG $\g=(\mb{V,E})$
output: Set of possible expressions for $f(\mb{y} \,|\, do(\mb{x}), \mb{z})$, for any $f$ consistent with $\g$
nodes.statement_short: Like CIDM, but instead of failing it orients the first undirected edge of a shortest offending path both ways and recurses, returning a multiset of expressions.
nodes.label: alg:cida-meek1

nodes.name: Concatenation of paths
nodes.statement: We denote the concatenation of paths by the symbol $\oplus$, so that for a path $p = \langle X_1,X_2, \dots, X_m \rangle$, $p = p(X_1, X_r) \oplus p(X_r, X_m)$, for $1\le r\le m$.

nodes.name: Bucket Decomposition
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (\textbf{Bucket Decomposition}; \citealp{perkovic2020identifying})}
    Let $\mb{D}$ be a node set in an MPDAG $\g$. Then $\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k}$, $k \ge 1$, is the bucket decomposition of $\mb{D}$ in $\g$ if $\mb{B_i}$, $i \in \{ 1, \dots, k\}$, is a bucket in $\mb{D}$ and $\cup_{i=1}^k \mb{B_i} = \mb{D}$.
nodes.label: def:bucket-decomp

nodes.name: Distance to Z
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (\textbf{Distance to $\mb{Z}$}; \citealp{perkovic2017interpreting})} 
    Let $\{X,Y\}$ and $\mb{Z}$ be disjoint node sets in an MPDAG $\g$, and let $p$ be a path in $\g$ from $X$ to $Y$ such that $\g$ has a possibly directed path (possibly of zero length) from every collider on $p$ to $\mb{Z}$. Further, let $\{C_1, \dots, C_k\}$ be the set of colliders on $p$, and let $\ell_i$, $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, be the length of a shortest possibly directed path in $\g$ from $C_i$ to $\mb{Z}$. Then the \emph{distance to $\mb{Z}$} for $p$ is $\sum_{i=1}^k \ell_i$.
nodes.statement_short: For a path whose colliders all reach Z by possibly directed paths, the sum of their shortest possibly-directed distances to Z.
nodes.label: def:distance

nodes.name: Rules of the do Calculus
assumptions: $\mb{X,Y,Z,}$ and $\mb{W}$ be pairwise disjoint (possibly empty) node sets in a causal DAG $\g[D]$
nodes.statement_short: Pearl's three rules: delete observations, exchange actions and observations, delete actions, under d-separations in mutilated DAGs.
nodes.label: thm:do-calc

nodes.name: Pearl's Rule 1
nodes.statement: f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{z,w}) = f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{w}).
nodes.label: thm:do-rule1

nodes.name: Pearl's Rule 2
nodes.statement: f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}),\mb{z},do(\mb{w})) = f(\mb{y} | \mb{x},\mb{z},do(\mb{w})).
nodes.label: thm:do-rule2

nodes.name: Pearl's Rule 3
nodes.statement:
\begin{split}
            f(\mb{y} | do(\mb{x}), \mb{z}, do(\mb{w})) = f(\mb{y} | \mb{z}, do(\mb{w})), \end{split}
nodes.label: thm:do-rule3

nodes.name: Conditional expectation of a multivariate Gaussian
nodes.label: lem:mardia

nodes.name: Wright's Rule
conclusions: $\mathrm{Cov}(X_i, X_j) = \sum_{r=1}^s \pi_r$
nodes.statement_short: In a standardized linear SEM, a covariance equals the sum over collider-free paths of the products of edge coefficients.
nodes.label: lem:wright

nodes.name: Covariance in a linear SEM via causal paths
nodes.origin_citation: Henckel et al. 2022, proof of Lemma B.4
nodes.statement_short: Each variable is a sum of ancestors' errors weighted by total causal-path effects; covariances sum over common ancestors.
nodes.label: lem:sem-covariance

nodes.name: Local Markov property characterization
nodes.origin_citation: Lauritzen et al. 1990, Theorem 1 and Proposition 3
assumptions: $f$ be an observational density over $\mb{V}$
nodes.label: lem:markov-equiv

nodes.name: Edges oriented by adding an orientation point to descendants
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (cf.\ Lemma F.1 of \citealp{rothenhausler2018causal})}
    Let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in an MPDAG $\g = (\mb{V,E})$ such that $X - Y$ is in $\g$. Let $\g'$ be an MPDAG constructed from $\g$ by adding $X \to Y$ and completing the orientation rules R1 - R4 of \cite{meek1995causal}. For any $Z,W \in \mb{V}$, if $Z - W$ is in $\g$ and $Z \rightarrow W$ is in $\g'$, then $W \in \mathrm{De}(Y,\g')$.
assumptions: $X - Y$ is in $\g$
$Z - W$ is in $\g$ and $Z \rightarrow W$ is in $\g'$
conclusions: $W \in \mathrm{De}(Y,\g')$
nodes.label: lem:adding-edges-imply

nodes.name: Orienting undirected edges out of a node yields an MPDAG
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (cf.\ Lemma F.2 of \citealp{rothenhausler2018causal})}
    Let $X$ be a node in an MPDAG $\g=(\mb{V}, \mb{E})$, and let $\mb{S}$ be a set such that for all $S \in \mb{S}$, $X - S$ is in $\g$. Then there is an MPDAG $\g' = (\mb{V}, \mb{E'})$ that is formed by taking $\g$, orienting $X \to S$ for all $S \in \mb{S}$, and completing R1-R4 of \cite{meek1995causal}.
nodes.label: lem:undirected-imply

nodes.name: Meek's Lemma 1 for CPDAGs
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (cf.\ Lemma 1 of \citealp{meek1995causal})}
    Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be nodes in a CPDAG $\g[C]$. If $\g[C]$ contains $X \to Y - Z$, then $\g[C]$ contains $X \to Y$.
assumptions: $\g[C]$ contains $X \to Y - Z$
conclusions: $\g[C]$ contains $X \to Y$
nodes.label: lem:prop1meek

nodes.name: PCO Algorithm
output: List of buckets $\mb{B} {=} (\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k}), k \ge 1$, in $\mb{D}$ given $\g$
nodes.statement_short: Repeatedly peel off a bucket of V with all boundary edges pointing into it, prepending its intersection with D to the output list.
nodes.label: alg:pco

nodes.name: Causal path in some DAG implies possibly causal
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (Lemma 3.2 of \citealp{perkovic2017interpreting})}
    Let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in an MPDAG $\g$ and let $p$ be a path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$. If there exists a DAG $\g[D] \in [\g]$ such that the path in $\g[D]$ corresponding to $p$ in $\g$ is causal, then $p$ is possibly causal.
assumptions: there exists a DAG $\g[D] \in [\g]$ such that the path in $\g[D]$ corresponding to $p$ in $\g$ is causal
conclusions: $p$ is possibly causal
nodes.label: lem:pc-imply1b

nodes.name: Possibly causal definite status paths
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (Lemma 3.5 of \citealp{perkovic2017interpreting})}
    Let $p = \langle V_1, \dots, V_k \rangle$, $k \ge 2$, be a definite status path in an MPDAG. Then $p$ is possibly causal if and only if $p$ has no edge $V_i \gets V_{i+1}$ for any $i \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$.
conclusions: $p$ is possibly causal if and only if $p$ has no edge $V_i \gets V_{i+1}$ for any $i \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$
equivalent_conditions: $p$ has no edge $V_i \gets V_{i+1}$ for any $i \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$
nodes.label: lem:pc-def-stat

nodes.name: PCO output consists of ordered buckets
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (Lemma 3.5 of \citealp{perkovic2020identifying})}
    Let $\mb{D}$ be a node set in an MPDAG $\g$ and let $\mathrm{PCO}(\mb{D}, \g)=(\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k})$, $k \ge 1$, be the output of the PCO Algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:pco}). Then for $i,j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, $\mb{B_i}$ and $\mb{B_j}$ are buckets in $\mb{D}$, and if $i < j$, then $\mb{B_i} < \mb{B_j}$ in $\g$.
nodes.label: lem:PCO-buckets

nodes.name: Causal path into a bucket reaches all its nodes
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (Lemma C.2 of \citealp{perkovic2020identifying})}
    Let $\mb{C}$ be a bucket in $\mb{V}$ in an MPDAG $\g = (\mb{V},\mb{E})$ and let $X \in \mb{V} \setminus \mb{C}$. If there is a causal path from $X$ to $\mb{C}$ in $\g$, then for every node $C \in \mb{C}$, there is a causal path from $X$ to $C$ in $\g$.
assumptions: there is a causal path from $X$ to $\mb{C}$ in $\g$
conclusions: for every node $C \in \mb{C}$, there is a causal path from $X$ to $C$ in $\g$
nodes.label: lem:bucket-req1

nodes.name: Parent of a bucket is parent of all its nodes
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (cf. Proof of Lemma C.2 of \citealp{perkovic2020identifying})}
    Let $\mb{C}$ be a bucket in $\mb{V}$ in an MPDAG $\g = (\mb{V},\mb{E})$ and let $X \in \mb{V} \setminus \mb{C}$. If $X \in \mathrm{Pa}(\mb{C}, \g)$, then $X \in \mathrm{Pa}(C, \g)$ for every node $C \in \mb{C}$.
assumptions: $X \in \mathrm{Pa}(\mb{C}, \g)$
conclusions: $X \in \mathrm{Pa}(C, \g)$ for every node $C \in \mb{C}$
nodes.label: lem:bucket-req2

nodes.name: No undirected-start possibly causal path to An(Y)
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (Lemma D.1(i) of \citealp{perkovic2020identifying})}
    Let $\mb{X}$ and $\mb{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in an MPDAG $\g =(\mb{V,E})$, where there is no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mb{Y}$ that starts with an undirected edge in $\g$. Then there is no proper possibly causal path from $\mb{X}$ to $\mathrm{An}(\mb{Y},\g_{\mb{V} \setminus \mb{X}})$ that starts with an undirected edge in $\g$.
nodes.label: lem:xtod

nodes.name: Shortest subsequence of a possibly causal path
nodes.statement:
{\normalfont (cf.\ Lemma 3.6 of \citealp{perkovic2017interpreting})}
    Let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct nodes in an MPDAG $\g$ and let $p$ be a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$. Then any shortest subsequence of $p$ in $\g$ forms an unshielded, possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$.
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
assumptions: $p$ be a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$
conclusions: any shortest subsequence of $p$ in $\g$ forms an unshielded, possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$
nodes.label: lem:shortest-subseq

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 24
nodes.statement: Let $k$ be the number of nodes on $p$. Pick an arbitrary shortest subsequence of $p$ and call it $p^* :=\langle X=V_0, \dots, V_\ell=Y \rangle$, $0 < \ell \le k$. Note that there is no edge $V_i \gets V_j, 0 \le i < j \le k$ in $\g$, since this would contradict that $p$ is possibly causal. Thus, $p^*$ is also possibly causal. Further, note that $p^*$ is unshielded, since if any triple on the path is shielded, it either contradicts that $p^*$ is possibly causal (i.e., $V_i \gets V_{i+2}$ cannot be in $p^*$) or that $p^*$ is a shortest subsequence of $p$ (i.e., $V_i \to V_{i+2}$ and $V_i - V_{i+2}$ cannot be in $p^*$).
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
nodes.statement_short: A backward edge on the subsequence would contradict p possibly causal; a shielded triple would contradict minimality or possible causality.

nodes.name: Possibly causal iff no backward directed paths
nodes.statement: Let $p=\langle P_0, \dots, P_k \rangle$ be a path in an MPDAG $\g$. Then $p$ is possibly causal if and only if $\g$ does not contain any path $P_i \gets \dots \gets P_j$, $0 \le i < j \le k$.
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
conclusions: $p$ is possibly causal if and only if $\g$ does not contain any path $P_i \gets \dots \gets P_j$, $0 \le i < j \le k$
equivalent_conditions: $\g$ does not contain any path $P_i \gets \dots \gets P_j$, $0 \le i < j \le k$
nodes.label: lem:nobackpaths

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 25
nodes.statement:
$\Leftarrow$ Follows immediately.
    $\Rightarrow$ Let $p$ be possibly causal, and for sake of contradiction, suppose $\g$ contains a path $q$ from $P_i$ to $P_j$, $0 \le i < j \le k$, of the form $P_i=Q_0 \gets \dots \gets Q_{\ell} =P_j$. Then define $r=\langle P_i = R_0, \dots, R_m= P_j\rangle$ to be a shortest subsequence of $p(P_i,P_j)$ in $\g$, and note that by Lemma \ref{lem:shortest-subseq}, $r$ is an unshielded, possibly causal path.

    To see that $r(R_0, R_1)$ takes the form $R_0 - R_1$, note that $\g$ cannot contain $R_0 \gets R_1$, since $r$ is possibly causal. Further, $\g$ cannot contain $R_0 \to R_1$, since $r$ being unshielded would imply, by R1 of \cite{meek1995causal}, that $\g$ contains the cycle $P_i= R_0 \to \dots \to R_m=P_j=Q_{\ell} \to \dots \to Q_0=P_i$. Then since $\g$ contains $R_0 - R_1$, there must be a DAG $\g[D] \in [\g]$ that contains $R_0 \to R_1$. But since $r$ is unshielded, this implies, by R1 of \cite{meek1995causal}, that $\g[D]$ contains the cycle $P_i= R_0 \to \dots \to R_m=P_j=Q_{\ell} \to \dots \to Q_0=P_i$, which is a contradiction.
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
nodes.statement_short: A backward directed path plus an unshielded possibly causal subsequence forces a directed cycle via Meek's R1 in some DAG of [G].

nodes.name: Concatenation of causal and possibly causal paths
nodes.statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be distinct nodes in an MPDAG $\g$.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If $p$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ and $q$ is a causal path from $Y$ to $Z$, then $p \oplus q$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Z$.

        \item If $p$ is a causal path from $X$ to $Y$ and $q$ is a possibly causal path from $Y$ to $Z$, then $p \oplus q$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Z$.
    \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths

assumptions: $p$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ and $q$ is a causal path from $Y$ to $Z$
conclusions: $p \oplus q$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Z$

assumptions: $p$ is a causal path from $X$ to $Y$ and $q$ is a possibly causal path from $Y$ to $Z$
conclusions: $p \oplus q$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Z$
$p \oplus q$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Z$
assumptions: $p$ is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ and $q$ is a causal path from $Y$ to $Z$
$p$ is a causal path from $X$ to $Y$ and $q$ is a possibly causal path from $Y$ to $Z$
nodes.label: lem:concat

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 26
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
nodes.statement_short: Show p and q share only Y and no backward edge joins them, each by contradiction via Lemma 25 and Meek's R1 cycles.

nodes.name: Possibly causal paths need not be causal in any DAG of [G]
nodes.statement:
Perhaps contrary to intuition, even if a path is possibly causal in an MPDAG $\g$, there may not exist a DAG in $[\g]$ where the corresponding path is causal.
    
    To see this, consider the MPDAG $\g$ in Figure \ref{fig:pc-imply1a} and let $p = \langle X, V_1, V_2, Y \rangle$. Note that $p$ is possibly causal. Let $\g[D]$ be an arbitrary DAG in $\g$ and define $p^*$ to be the path in $\g[D]$ corresponding to $p$ in $\g$. If $p^*$ begins $X \gets V_1$, it is non-causal. Thus, consider when $p^*$ begins $X \to V_1$. It follows that $\g[D]$ contains $V_1 \to V_2$ by R1 of \cite{meek1995causal} as well as $V_2 \gets Y$ by R4 of \cite{meek1995causal}, so that again, $p^*$ is non-causal.
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
nodes.statement_short: A possibly causal path in an MPDAG may be non-causal in every represented DAG, shown via Meek's R1 and R4.
nodes.label: rem:pc-imply1a

nodes.name: Possibly causal path iff causal path in some DAG
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in an MPDAG $\g$. Then there is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$ if and only if there is at least one DAG in $[\g]$ with a causal path from $X$ to $Y$.
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
conclusions: there is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$ if and only if there is at least one DAG in $[\g]$ with a causal path from $X$ to $Y$
equivalent_conditions: there is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$
there is at least one DAG in $[\g]$ with a causal path from $X$ to $Y$
nodes.label: lem:pc-imply2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 28
nodes.statement:
$\Leftarrow$ Holds by Lemma \ref{lem:pc-imply1b}.
    $\Rightarrow$ Let $p$ be a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ and let $p^*=\langle X=V_0, \dots, V_k=Y \rangle$, $k \ge 1$, be a shortest subsequence of $p$ in $\g$. By Lemma \ref{lem:shortest-subseq}, $p^*$ forms an unshielded, possibly causal path. Since $p^*$ is possibly causal, $\g$ must contain $V_0 \to V_1$ or $V_0 - V_1$. Thus, there is a DAG $\g[D] \in [\g]$ that contains the edge $V_0 \to V_1$. Further, since $p^*$ is unshielded, $\g[D]$ contains $X=V_0 \to \dots \to V_k=Y$ by R1 of \cite{meek1995causal}.
nodes.section: C.1 Results on Possibly Causal Paths
nodes.statement_short: One direction is Lemma 18; for the other orient the first edge of an unshielded shortest subsequence and propagate with Meek's R1.

nodes.name: PCO output is an ordered bucket decomposition
nodes.statement: Note that the output of the PCO Algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:pco}) is an ordered bucket decomposition (Definition \ref{def:obd}) of the input node set in the input MPDAG. This follows from the steps of Algorithm \ref{alg:pco} and Lemma \ref{lem:PCO-buckets}.
nodes.section: C.2 Remarks on the Ordering of Buckets

nodes.name: Bucket Decomposition Matching
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{D}$ be a node set in an MPDAG $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$. Let $(\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k}), k \ge 1$, be an ordered bucket decomposition of $\mb{D}$ in $\g$ (Definition \ref{def:obd}), and let $(\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_{\ell}})$, $\ell \ge k$, be an ordered bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$. We say that $(\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_{\ell}})$ is an ordered bucket decomposition that \emph{matches the ordering} of $(\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k})$ if the following holds. For any $i,j \in \{1, \dots, k \}$ and $m, n \in \{ 1, \dots, \ell \}$ such that $\mb{B_i} \cap \mb{C_m} \neq \emptyset$ and $\mb{B_j} \cap \mb{C_n} \neq \emptyset$, if $\mb{B_i} < \mb{B_j}$, then $\mb{C_m} < \mb{C_n}$.
nodes.section: C.2 Remarks on the Ordering of Buckets
nodes.statement_short: An ordered bucket decomposition of V matches one of D if the order of buckets of D is respected by the buckets of V containing them.
nodes.label: def:obd-matching

nodes.name: Existence of a matching ordered bucket decomposition of V
nodes.statement: Let $\mb{D}$ be a node set in the MPDAG $\g = (\mb{V}, \mb{E})$, and let $PCO(\mb{D}, \g) =(\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k})$, $k \ge 1$, be the output of the PCO Algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:pco}). Since the algorithm relies on the intersection of $\mb{D}$ with an ordering of the bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$, there must exist an ordered bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$ (Definition \ref{def:obd}) that matches the ordering (Definition \ref{def:obd-matching}) of $(\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k})$.
nodes.section: C.2 Remarks on the Ordering of Buckets
nodes.label: rem:obd-matching

nodes.name: Possibly causal path between buckets contains a causal subsequence
nodes.statement: Let $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ be an MPDAG, and let $\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_{\ell}}$, $\ell \ge 1$, be the bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$ (Definition \ref{def:bucket-decomp}). Further, let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in $\g$ such that $X \in \mb{C_x}$ and $Y \in \mb{C_y}$ for some $x,y \in \{1, \dots, \ell\}$, $x \neq y$. If $p = \langle X=P_0, \dots, P_k=Y\rangle, k \ge 1$, is a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{C_x}$ to $\mb{C_y}$ in $\g$, then $\g$ contains a subsequence of $p$ that is a causal path from $X$ to $Y$.
nodes.section: C.3 Results on Paths Among Buckets
assumptions: $p = \langle X=P_0, \dots, P_k=Y\rangle, k \ge 1$, is a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{C_x}$ to $\mb{C_y}$ in $\g$
conclusions: $\g$ contains a subsequence of $p$ that is a causal path from $X$ to $Y$
nodes.label: lem:bucket-req3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 32
nodes.statement:
Let $p = \langle X=P_0, \dots, P_k=Y\rangle, k \ge 1$, be a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{C_x}$ to $\mb{C_y}$ in $\g$. Since $p$ is proper, $X$ is the only node in $\mb{C_x}$ on $p$. Thus $P_1$ is the first node in the bucket $\mb{C_a}$ where $a \in \{1, \dots, \ell \} \setminus \{x\}$. By the definition of buckets and the fact that $p$ is possibly causal, $p$ contains $X \to P_1$. Then by Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-req2}, $\g$ contains $X \to A$ for all $A \in \mb{C_a}$.

    When $Y \in \mb{C_a}$, $\g$ contains the subsequence $X \to Y$ and we are done. When $Y \notin \mb{C_a}$, define $P_q$, $q \in \{1, \dots, k \}$, to be the last node on $p$ in $\mb{C_a}$. Note that $\g$ contains $X \to P_q$ and consider the node $P_{q+1}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-restrict1}, $p(P_1, P_q)$ is entirely contained in $\mb{C_a}$. Thus, $P_{q+1}$ is the first node in the bucket $\mb{C_b}$ where $b \in \{1, \dots, \ell\} \setminus \{a, x\}$. By the definition of buckets and the fact that $p$ is possibly causal, $p$ contains $P_q \to P_{q+1}$. Then by Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-req2}, $\g$ contains $P_q \to B$ for all $B \in \mb{C_b}$.

    When $Y \in \mb{C_b}$, $\g$ contains the subsequence $X \to P_q \to Y$ and we are done. When $Y \notin \mb{C_b}$, we can continue in this way until we reach the first node in $\mb{C_y}$---call it $P_{r+1}$. By the same logic as above, $p$ must contain $P_r \to P_{r+1}$, where $P_r \notin \mb{C_y}$ and where $\g$ contains $X \to P_q \to \dots \to P_r$. So again by Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-req2}, $\g$ contains $P_r \to W$ for all $W \in \mb{C_y}$ and thus $\g$ contains the subsequence $X \to P_q \to \dots \to P_r \to Y$.
nodes.section: C.3 Results on Paths Among Buckets
nodes.statement_short: Walk p bucket by bucket; at each bucket exit Lemma 22 gives a directed edge to every node of the next bucket, building a causal subsequence.

nodes.name: Possibly causal paths stay inside a bucket
nodes.statement: Let $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ be an MPDAG, and let $\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_k}, k \ge 1$, be the bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$ (Definition \ref{def:bucket-decomp}). If $X, Y \in \mb{C_i}$, $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, then there is no possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$ containing nodes in $\mb{V} \setminus \mb{C_i}$.
nodes.section: C.3 Results on Paths Among Buckets
assumptions: $X, Y \in \mb{C_i}$, $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$
conclusions: there is no possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$ containing nodes in $\mb{V} \setminus \mb{C_i}$
nodes.label: lem:bucket-restrict1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 33
nodes.statement:
For sake of contradiction, suppose that there is a possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$ containing nodes in $\mb{V} \setminus \mb{C_i}$---call this path $p=\langle X=P_0, \dots, P_u=Y \rangle$, $u \ge 1$. Let $P_s$, $s \in \{1, \dots, u-1\}$, be an arbitrary node on $p$ such that $P_s \in \mb{V} \setminus \mb{C_i}$. Let $P_r$, $r \in \{0, \dots, s-1\}$ be the node on $p$ closest to $P_s$ such that $P_r \in \mb{C_i}$. And let $P_t$, $t \in \{s+1, \dots, u\}$ be the node on $p$ closest to $P_s$ such that $P_t \in \mb{C_i}$.

    By the definition of $P_t$, we have that $P_{t-1} \notin \mb{C_i}$ and $P_t \in \mb{C_i}$. Consider the edge between $P_{t-1}$ and $P_t$. Since $\mb{C_i}$ is a maximal undirected connected subset of $\mb{V}$, then $p$ does not contain $P_{t-1} - P_t$. Further since $p$ is possibly causal, it does not contain $P_{t-1} \gets P_t$. Therefore $p$ must contain $P_{t-1} \to P_t$. But then by Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-req2}, $\g$ must contain $P_{t-1} \to P_r$, which contradicts that $p$ is possibly causal.
nodes.section: C.3 Results on Paths Among Buckets
nodes.statement_short: Re-entering the bucket uses a directed edge, and Lemma 22 then gives a backward edge contradicting possible causality.

nodes.name: No possibly causal path from later to earlier buckets
nodes.statement: Let $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ be an MPDAG and let $(\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_k}), k \ge 1$, be an ordered bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$ (Definition \ref{def:obd}). Then for any $i, j \in \{1, \dots, k\}, i < j$, there is no possibly causal path from $\mb{C_j}$ to $\mb{C_i}$ in $\g$.
nodes.section: C.3 Results on Paths Among Buckets
conclusions: there is no possibly causal path from $\mb{C_j}$ to $\mb{C_i}$ in $\g$
nodes.label: lem:bucket-restrict2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 34
nodes.statement:
For sake of contradiction, let there be a possibly causal path from $\mb{C_j}$ to $\mb{C_i}$ in $\g$. Choose a shortest such path $p :=\langle P_0, \dots, P_u \rangle$, $u \ge 1$, and let $\mb{S}$ be the smallest collection of buckets in $\mb{V}$ such that every node on $p$ is in one bucket in $\mb{S}$. Consider the order in which $p$ enters and exits each bucket in $\mb{S}$. $p$ begins in $\mb{C_j}$, but once it exits $\mb{C_j}$, it never returns. This holds by Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-restrict1} and the fact that $p$ is possibly causal. By the same logic, once $p$ enters any other bucket in $\mb{S}$, the first time it exits that bucket, it will never return. Thus, let $\mb{C_{\ell_1}}, \dots, \mb{C_{\ell_m}}$, $1 < m \le k$, be an arrangement of the buckets in $\mb{S}$ in order of their appearance on $p$.
    
    Note that $P_0$ is the only node on $p$ in $\mb{C_j}$ by the choice of $p$ as a shortest path. Therefore, $p$ is a proper possibly causal path from $\mb{C_j}$ to $\mb{C_i}$. It follows by Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-req3} and the choice of $p$ as a shortest path that $p$ is causal. Based on the existence of this causal path, any partial causal ordering of $\mb{V}$ consistent with $\g$ must require $\mb{C_{\ell_1}} < \dots < \mb{C_{\ell_m}}$. Since $\ell_1 = j$ and $\ell_m = i$ by the definition of $p$, then any partial causal ordering of $\mb{V}$ consistent with $\g$ must require $\mb{C_j} < \mb{C_i}$. But this contradicts the definition of $(\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_k})$ as an ordered bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g$, where $\mb{C_i} < \mb{C_j}$.
nodes.section: C.3 Results on Paths Among Buckets
nodes.statement_short: A shortest such path is proper and hence causal (Lemma 32), forcing C_j before C_i in any partial causal ordering.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 35
nodes.statement: Let $(\mb{C_1}, \dots, \mb{C_{\ell}})$, $\ell \ge k$, be the ordered bucket decomposition of $\mb{V}$ in $\g=(\mb{V},\mb{E})$ that matches the ordering of $(\mb{B_1}, \dots, \mb{B_k})$ (see Remark \ref{rem:obd-matching}). Let $\mb{B_i} \cap \mb{C_m} \neq \emptyset$ and $\mb{B_j} \cap \mb{C_n} \neq \emptyset$, where $m,n \in \{1, \dots, \ell\}$. By construction, $m<n$. If there were a possibly causal path from $B_j \in \mb{B_j}$ to $B_i \in \mb{B_i}$ in $\g$, then there would be a possibly causal path from $B_j \in \mb{C_n}$ to $B_i \in \mb{C_m}$ in $\g$, which contradicts Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-restrict2}.

nodes.statement_short: Lift to the matching ordered bucket decomposition of V and apply Lemma 34.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 36
nodes.statement: For sake of contradiction, suppose there is a DAG in $[\g]$ with a causal path $p$ from $\mb{C_j}$ to $\mb{C_i}$. Then by Lemma \ref{lem:pc-imply1b}, the path in $\g$ corresponding to $p$ is possibly causal from $\mb{C_j}$ to $\mb{C_i}$, which contradicts Lemma \ref{lem:bucket-restrict2}.

nodes.statement_short: A causal path in a DAG of [G] is possibly causal in G (Lemma 18), contradicting Lemma 34.

Then by Lemma \ref{lem:pc-imply1b}, the path in $\g$ corresponding to $p$ is possibly causal from $\mb{B_j}$ to $\mb{B_i}$, which contradicts Corollary \ref{cor:bucket-restrict2a}.

nodes.name: Setup for Proof of Lemma 38(i): structure of shortest d-connecting paths
nodes.statement:
Let $\mb{N}$, $\mb{H}$, $\mb{X'}$, $\mb{B}$, and $\mb{P}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in an MPDAG $\g =(\mb{V,E})$, and let $\g[D]$ be a DAG in $[\g]$. Suppose there is a path from $\mb{B}$ to $\mb{N} \cup \mb{H}$ that is d-connecting given $\mb{X'} \cup \mb{P}$ in $\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X'}\mb{N'}}\underline{\mb{H}}}$, where $\mb{N'}$ is a node set in $\g$ such that $\mb{N'} \subseteq \mb{N}$ and $\mb{N'} \cap \mathrm{An}(\mb{P},\g[D]_{\overline{\mb{X'}}}) = \emptyset$. Let $p_1 =\langle B, \dots, N \rangle$, $B \in \mb{B}$, $N \in \mb{N} \cup \mb{H}$, be a shortest such path, and let $p^*$ and $p_2$ be the corresponding paths in $\g$ and $\g[D]$, respectively. Finally, let $q_1 = \langle Q_0, \dots, Q_k \rangle$, $k \ge 1$, be a subpath of $p_1$, and let $q^*$ and $q_2$ be the corresponding paths in $\g$ and $\g[D]$, respectively.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If $q^*$ is undirected, then $q_2$ does not contain a collider on $p_2$.

        \item If $q^*$ is undirected and $Q_k \notin \mb{H}$, then $q^*$ and $(-q^*)$ are possibly causal.

        \item If $q_1$ is causal and $q^*$ begins with $Q_0 \to Q_1$, then $q^*$ is causal.

        \item If $q_1$ contains at least one collider and $q^*$ begins with $Q_0 \to Q_1$, then $\g$ contains a causal path from $Q_0$ to $\mb{P}$.
    \end{enumerate}
